elements.element: Audit no more than once per 12 months
elements.evidence: "shall be conducted no more than once in any twelve (12) month period"
"Any such audit shall be permitted by Licensee within 30 days of Licensee's receipt of a written request of Licensor" — written request plus a 30-day window Licensee may use
"an independent Certified Public Accountant or other Audit Professional"
"and bound by written obligations of confidentiality"

elements.element: Vendor bears audit cost unless underpayment/discrepancy exceeds 5%
elements.evidence: "cost of the audit will be borne by Licensor unless a discrepancy of more than five-percent (5%) is discovered"

elements.element: No direct access to Customer systems
elements.evidence: "without access to Licensee's systems or networks"
"no more than once in any twelve (12) month period"
"within 30 days of Licensee's receipt of a written request of Licensor"

elements.element: Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10%
elements.evidence: "unless a discrepancy of more than five-percent (5%) is discovered" — threshold is 5%, not 10%

reasons: All seven preferred atomic elements are now express in the operative text: frequency cap, written request with a 30-day window, business hours, independent auditor, auditor confidentiality, Licensor-borne cost subject to the 5% discrepancy trigger, and no system access.

Fallback is not independently satisfied because its 10% cost-shift threshold is absent (the clause uses 5%), but that is the preferred figure and the locked target is preferred, so this is immaterial.

Minimality fails the official gate: operation 1 expands 6 words to 13 and operation 2 expands 20 words to 47. Tighter wording is available — "bound by confidentiality" instead of "bound by written obligations of confidentiality", and "Licensee's systems" instead of "Licensee's systems or networks".

Intent is preserved: the cost-allocation sentence and the mutual-selection mechanic are untouched, no undefined terms are introduced, and the added constraints attach cleanly to the existing audit right.

Note in the rationale (not a deviation) that the 30-day mechanic is a deadline to permit the audit rather than an express advance-notice period; a one-word change to "no earlier than 30 days after" would align it exactly with the playbook.
